llm.summary: This is an offline output-registration helper that writes a local ledger; I found no hidden network behavior, privilege escalation, or deceptive persistence.

dimensions.detail: Read, Bash, and Write are proportionate for hashing files and writing a local ledger; WebFetch is listed even though the core tool is documented as offline, so it is broader than necessary but not used by the script.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is via the skills CLI from a GitHub path or manual git clone and copy into an agent skills directory; this is disclosed and typical, but users should verify the source/tag before installing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill is mostly Chinese-language and includes a broad trigger term, but its runtime instructions stay focused on output registration and explicitly warn users not to register sensitive raw content.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The only persistence found is local registry output under registry/ in md, csv, and jsonl formats; there are no services, scheduled tasks, shell hooks, credential reads, or cross-session backdoor behavior.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to register AI outputs for provenance and integrity using SHA-256 hashes, model/version metadata, prompt hash, timestamps, issuer, and license; the inspected script implements add, verify, lookup, and report around local registry files.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with a Chinese-language local CLI that records hashes and short summaries of outputs into local registry files. Avoid registering secrets, confidential text, or internal identifiers, because the ledger can preserve a summary and metadata for later lookup.
llm.findings:
[AE1] unexpected: I inspected the full local SKILL.md, README.md, LICENSE.md, and related files; the flagged text is a license-scope notice, not evidence of analysis evasion or an unavailable payload.
[SQP-1] expected: The short trigger term could cause over-invocation, but the capability it activates is a local ledger workflow and does not show high-impact automatic action.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-language documentation, CLI messages, metadata, and sample registry entries are present; this is a usability/localization concern, not a security concern in the inspected artifacts.
